decisions.reason: Step 2.2 used smooth kernel/cokernel representatives not supplied by F1’s stated index interface. Added the existing published lem-chiral-dirac-is-fredholm-with-kernel-and-cokernel as a direct dependency and F4; it identifies both Hilbert spaces with smooth opposite-chirality kernels on the closed four-manifold. The explicit Clifford construction, harmonic calibration b1−1−b_minus, adjoint trace ch(G)=3−4c2, multiplicity two and real complexification then give the unchanged index formula. This is a dependency_citation defect, not a false index formula.

The conclusion is already supplied by F4 for the stated topology, but Proof 2.1 misidentifies the bound: perturbation values are uniformly H3-bounded, while the curvature equation on bounded smaller slice balls yields an H4 bound on solutions. Replaced the inaccurate phrase by that derivation and compact H4-to-H3 inclusion. Compact-set derivative control preserves surjectivity; finite cokernel directions and Sard prove density. This is a nonfatal explanatory defect because F4 directly proves the unchanged assertion.

F2’s full constructive proof supplies more than smoothness of a zero locus. In its Proof 4.1–6.1 the prepared section in range/obstruction coordinates is (u,g(u,z)+eta*alpha(z)) near zero, with alpha onto and Dg(0,0)=0. Its z derivative is eta*alpha at zero and stays onto after shrinking, by a bounded right inverse and the Neumann argument. The first range block is the identity, so the whole slice derivative is onto. For p=0 the obstruction target is zero and the range block already suffices. Away from the vertex the effective circle acts freely and its orbit direction lies in the kernel, so quotienting removes one kernel direction without altering surjectivity; index six becomes dimension five. Thus the protected punctured cone is regular before the middle perturbation. F4 supplies the regular ideal collar; middle transversality and compact support preserve both. The rejection’s general caution is correct but does not apply to this constructed perturbation.
